title: Ide burial tradition
description: The canon of Ana burial, Ebo Omunna, and Nde Eri continuity.
html:
IDE CANON OF ANA BURIAL, EBO OMUNNA, AND NDE ERI CONTINUITY

(Iwu Ini Ana, Ịchekwa Ebo Omunna, na Ncheta Nde Eri Ide)

PREAMBLE

Ana bu ndu. Mmili bu ndu. Nde eri anaghi ala n’efu.

This canon defines the lawful Ide way of burial, lineage preservation, and ancestral continuity, adaptable to both land clans and water clans, and binding on all Ide people.

ARTICLE I — SACRED DEFINITIONS

Ana — living earth

Mmili — sacred water, never a grave

Nde eri — ancestors

Omunna — lineage

Ebo Omunna — lineage essence (biological and spiritual)

Ịchekwa Ebo Omunna — rite of lineage preservation

Akpati Ana / Akpati — burial casket

Ize — tooth (Ide term)

Akpa-Nso — sealed lineage relic

Ndenka — Ide craft society

Uneri — ancestral museum and lineage vault

Uniku — clan centre

Okwu Eri — private family ancestral shrine

ARTICLE II — AKPATI ANA (BURIAL CASKET)

Only Akpati Ana is permitted.

Constructed solely from biodegradable woven fibre.

Metal, plastic, cement, chemical treatments, and embalming are forbidden.

ARTICLE III — FLOWERS

Flowers serve only for the honour and beautification of the Akpati.

Flowers carry no ritual or botanical continuity function.

ARTICLE IV — IN-GROUND BURIAL (MANDATORY)

Burial is always inside the ground.

Applicable to dry land and mangrove terrain by adjusting depth and soil layering.

The Akpati must never rest in standing water.

ARTICLE V — SEEDS, ROOTS, AND HERBS

Plant materials used need not be native, but must survive the burial environment.

Water clans and land clans select accordingly.

Families may choose herbs or other suitable small plants.

Burial grounds thus become living markers, not stone memorials.

ARTICLE VI — ỊCHEKWA EBO OMUNNA (LINEAGE PRESERVATION)

VI.1 Mandatory Extraction

One ize is removed for Uneri in all Ide burials.

VI.2 Optional Second Extraction

Families who establish an Okwu Eri may authorise the removal of a second ize.

VI.3 Ethics

This act is preservation, not mutilation.

No grave is ever reopened.

ARTICLE VII — NDENKA COMMISSIONS (PAID, PRE-BURIAL)

VII.1 Mandatory Craft for Uneri

The Akpa-Nso destined for Uneri must be crafted into ikenga by Ndenka as an artefact.

VII.2 Optional Family Commission

Families who can afford it may commission Ndenka to:

Create a private shrine object with the tooth inside the object to protect it

Used as a family artefact for Okwu Eri

VII.3 Timing of Payment

All payments to Ndenka must be completed before the burial.

No post-burial bargaining is permitted.

VII.4 Materials

Artefacts must be ceramic, stone, fired clay, or carved wood only.

ARTICLE VIII — UNERI (ANCESTRAL MUSEUM & VAULT)

Uneri is the central Ide lineage vault, located near Uniku.

It houses Ndenka-crafted artefacts containing preserved Ebo Omunna.

Artefacts are organised by clan, lineage, and generation.

Private ownership, sale, or export of Uneri artefacts is forbidden.

ARTICLE IX — OKWU ERI (OPTIONAL FAMILY SHRINE)

Okwu Eri is not mandatory.

It is reserved for families with the means to establish and maintain it.

It exists within the family home.

It houses Ndenka-crafted artefacts commissioned by the family.

It holds the second ize, distinct from the one kept in Uneri.
